OEM Partnerships: When to Embed vs Resell

OEM partnerships are agreements where one company embeds another’s product inside its own offering and sells it as part of a single package. They differ from reselling because the customer often never sees the underlying vendor. Sign one when the embedded capability is core to your value but not core to your roadmap, and the economics reward volume over margin.

Price the embed for scale, since the customer buys one package and margin is thin per unit. Model the deal at the partner’s real volume, not a hopeful one, because OEM math that works at a hundred customers can break at a thousand.
Signing an OEM deal that should have been a resell.
Pricing for margin instead of volume.
OEM only works at scale. A deal structured like a high-margin resell prices itself out of the volume that makes embedding worthwhile.
What is the difference between OEM and reselling?

A reseller sells the partner’s product as a distinct, branded thing the customer knows they are buying, while an OEM partner absorbs the capability into its own product and owns the customer relationship. The difference decides who owns support, pricing, and the customer.

Use it when the capability is core to your value but not core to your roadmap, the customer wants one product rather than two, and the economics reward volume over margin. If the customer needs to see the underlying vendor, resell instead.

Usually for volume, not margin, because the customer buys one package and the per-unit economics are thin. The deal has to be modeled at the partner’s real volume, since OEM math that works at small scale can lose money at large scale.

Thin margin if priced wrong, and strategic dependency on the embedded vendor’s pricing and roadmap. Both are managed in the contract through volume pricing, pricing protection, roadmap visibility, and a defined exit path.

Look at your next embed-or-resell decision and answer one question before anything else: who should own the customer relationship? If the answer is you, the model is OEM, and the work is to price it for volume and protect against the dependency you are about to take on.
